newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina says Q1 GDP up 8.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Argentina says Q1 GDP up 8.1 pct.

text.p: Argentina's gross domestic product grew by 8.1 percent in the first quarter of 1997, the Economy Ministry said Wednesday.
Gross fixed investment grew by 28.8 percent in the same period, it said.
The GDP growth figure compared with growth of 8.8 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 and a 3.2 percent contraction in the first quarter of last year.
Economists polled by Reuters had made an average forecast of 7.4 percent for first quarter growth.
First quarter growth was led by goods production, which expanded by 9.1 percent, driven by the farm sector, mining and manufacturing.
Expansion in gross fixed investment was propelled by a 36.7 percent rise in investment in machines and equipment and a 21.2 percent rise in construction investment.

On Tuesday, Dutch bank ING Barings said it upgraded its 1997 Argentine growth forecast to 6.6 percent from 5.2 percent. "The economy appears to be surging ahead, faster than we and most forecasters had anticipated," it said.
